audit.whatIsWrong: Stored chart read Skill/Sion/Sion/Skill/Skill/Sion/Sion. The packet is Garen for all six pre-item stages with Sion at two-plus items, and the page's own whys[] already said exactly that — whys[4] 'Level 6 your Demacian Justice execute keeps the lane in your favour', whys[5] 'First item you still snowball before his health stacking pays off'. Six rows were inverted against their own explanations. The two-plus-items rating of 5/10 also read as even while naming Sion the winner.
audit.why: Sion's lane damage is a telegraphed charge and a poke E; he has no way to win a short melee exchange against a free-cast Q reset plus Judgment, and no sustain against Perseverance. He takes over only once health stacking and Unstoppable Onslaught turn him into a teamfight body. Win rate 54.85% over 3136 games.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Garen through First item, Sion at two-plus items, with the final rating dropped to 3.5/10 to match the side. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike said to 'blow through his shield first' before executing, without naming what Glory in Death actually does. The late spike attributed his teamfight power vaguely to 'ult flank'.
audit.why: Glory in Death revives Sion with very rapid attacks that HEAL him and deal bonus damage based on the target's maximum health — so an R execute into an un-Grievous-Wounded Sion hands him a free healing window against the highest-HP target present. Unstoppable Onslaught is a 7500-range steerable charge whose knockup scales with distance travelled, and Garen owns no dash to break it.
audit.corrected: Level 6 spike now names Glory in Death and the Grievous Wounds requirement; late spike names Unstoppable Onslaught's range and distance scaling and tells the player to hold Flash for it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Decimating Smash was listed at an 8-second cooldown; Riot's value is 10/9/8/7/6, so 10s at rank 1 and 8s only at rank 3. Soul Furnace's reactivation window was never mentioned — Riot: 'shields himself and can reactivate after 3 seconds to deal Magic Damage to enemies nearby'. Most importantly, Roar of the Slayer appears nowhere in the interaction advice at all, despite reducing the armour of everything it passes through and knocking a minion back through you.
audit.why: Garen's entire damage output is physical: an empowered auto, Judgment ticks and item damage. An armour-shred E landing on him before the trade makes every subsequent point of Sion's damage land harder and is the actual reason his trades feel worse than the raw numbers suggest. Soul Furnace's 3-second delayed detonation is the other thing to count — walking away during the shield and returning after it has fired is the free trade. Both were absent.
audit.corrected: Roar of the Slayer's armour shred promoted to the tldr, focus and mistakes; Q re-stated at 10s rank 1; Soul Furnace's 3-second re-fire added to the all-in window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization already lists Executioner's Calling but nothing explains why, and nothing warns against the obvious tank-vs-tank instinct of stacking raw armour.
audit.why: Two of the three flagged missing interactions are itemization facts: Sion sustains through chip damage via Glory in Death so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades, and both Glory in Death and Soul Furnace scale off maximum health, so raw resistances are the wrong answer.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal requirement stated in the Level 6 spike and wants.you[2]; the max-health scaling stated in late and wants.foe[1].

edits.before: Track Sion’s Decimating Smash (Stun) (8s): Charged = knockup. Sidestep it. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Decimating Smash is 10s at rank 1, and only the fully charged swing knocks up — sidestep the wide end.

edits.before: Commit on Decimating Smash (Stun)’s cooldown, at your level/item spikes, and with jungle setup — bait his answer before you spend yours.
edits.after: Commit after Decimating Smash (10s at rank 1) is spent and Soul Furnace has already re-fired for its 3-second detonation.

edits.before: Eat a full Q stun. Fight into his W shield. Burn time on his E poke. The R buys fights, not poke — spend it like the last one in stock.
edits.after: Eating the fully charged Q. Fighting into a fresh Soul Furnace. Forgetting Roar of the Slayer cuts your armour, so his follow-up hits harder.

edits.before: : Sion changes the lane by forcing Garen to respect Sion Decimating Smash channel and furnace shield.
edits.after: Roar of the Slayer shreds your armour before he commits, so his real burst arrives after the E, not before.

edits.after: Roar of the Slayer shredding your armour first

edits.before: Demacian Justice executes a low Sion, but respect his passive — kill him too early and his zombie form still lands a charged Q and shoves, so blow through his shield first.
edits.after: Demacian Justice executes a low Sion, but Glory in Death revives him with rapid attacks that heal him and scale off your maximum health — bring Grievous Wounds before you spend R.

edits.before: Sion's tank build and long-range charged-Q engage make him the better team-fight piece, and his ult flank starts fights your Q slow alone can't peel.
edits.after: Unstoppable Onslaught charges from 7500 range and knocks up harder the further it travels — you own no dash, so hold Flash for that engage, not for the damage.

edits.before: Sion out-scales into a health-stacked tank whose long-range Q engage and ult flank make him the stronger team-fight body once two items are online.
edits.after: Sion out-scales into a health-stacker whose Soul Furnace and revived passive both scale off your maximum health — stacking raw armour is the wrong answer.

edits.after: Bring Grievous Wounds for his revive

edits.after: Scale damage off your max health

notes: UNVERIFIED, deliberately left in place: the page asserts in five separate fields (whys[0], whys[2], spikes[0].text, early, mid, wants.you[0]) that Garen's Q silence cancels Sion's charging Decimating Smash. Riot's text does not describe Q as a channel and the kit carries no channel flag, so whether a silence interrupts an in-progress charge is not answerable from the kit data. I did not edit those fields and did not assert the interaction anywhere new — but if it is wrong, the entire early-lane plan on this page rests on it and it should be checked. Also left alone: the missing-interactions file claims Unstoppable Onslaught 'cuts your retreat' with terrain. Riot's description says only that Sion charges and knocks up on collision, with no terrain creation, so per the trust-the-description rule I wrote the range and distance-scaling knockup instead of a terrain claim.
